prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based therapy for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B003 prize for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Having read the full first-round exchange, I find that the case rests on the same points that all six of us gave independently, and not on the unanimous opening ranking. The chain runs from the incretin effect and the native physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action (Holst), through proglucagon processing, receptor biology and the wider actions of the peptide (Drucker), to the identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form (Mojsov). It ends in therapies with replicated, large randomized-trial effects on glycaemia, body weight and, increasingly, cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The mechanism is stable and independently confirmed and the clinical effect is mature, so recognition is neither premature nor speculative. Framing the citation around the physiology and the active peptide, with the therapies named as the consequence, gives a bounded achievement that three people can carry, and it is a framing I can defend in public.
statement.case_against: The case against is still attribution, not merit. Knudsen's long-acting analogues are what patients actually receive, and the three-name cap forces a judgement between discovery and engineering. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide relative to Habener and other early peptide investigators is contested, and none of us, including me, can settle it from the supplied files. Everyone's reading of that dispute rests on recalled and unverified knowledge, and a prize that rests on it needs a careful citation that does not overclaim a single origin of GLP-1 biology. A reader could also say that the therapy is the achievement and that we honoured only its antecedents. I accept that this is a visible omission, and the committee should say openly that it made this choice on the criterion of discovery.

responses.point: He argued that Knudsen's exclusion is not cost-free, that her claim is at least as strong as Mojsov's if the citation is framed around therapy, and that the committee must make the discovery-versus-therapy judgement openly. He also kept B045 as a strong later candidate but not a competitor to B003 because its medical impact is mostly indirect.
responses.response: I agree with him that the exclusion has a cost and that the framing decides everything. If the committee framed the part around the therapy, Knudsen's claim would be at least as strong as Mojsov's and my trio would be the wrong one. I do not frame it that way. The physiology and the identification of the active form are what the three names stand for, and Knudsen's programme is the engineering built on that target. I would put this into the committee's own record of the deliberation and not leave it as an unstated default. On B045 I accept his point that it does not match B003 on direct therapeutic consequence, and I have moved to treat it as a clean fallback and not a rival. My earlier argument about diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer shows relevance, not an established clinical effect, and I will not lean on it harder than that.

responses.point: She asked me, as chair, to say what evidence would settle Mojsov's standing, and said she would accept Knudsen only if the part were reframed as physiology plus drug design and Mojsov were dropped. She also ranks B034 as her second alternative and would accept a mechanism-only prize with Chen and Barber.
responses.response: This is the right question, and I cannot answer it from the files we have. What would settle it is the primary record: the dated publications and the experimental data showing who first isolated, sequenced and demonstrated the insulinotropic activity of the truncated GLP-1(7-36) form, and who first synthesized it, together with Habener's group's own contemporaneous reports. Without that, the committee should state that Mojsov's inclusion rests on her identification and synthesis of the active form being a defined, testable step, and that the citation is worded so that it does not claim a sole origin. If the priority review contradicted that step, I would reopen the third name, and I would then take her suggestion of Knudsen seriously. I would not do it by default. On B034, I agree that Chen and Barber is the more defensible pair, but a mechanism-only prize can wait while a therapy-linked achievement is available.

responses.point: He accepted the Knudsen argument as the most serious challenge to the trio but would not swap her in, and he disagreed with my ranking of B045 on the ground that its link to disease and treatment is thinner than for B003, B018 or B043. He also doubted a two-part prize because it would push the GLP-1 group below three people.
responses.response: I agree that the Knudsen question is the most serious challenge, and we reach the same answer by the same route. On B045 I accept his point that the clinical link is thinner. That is why I will not offer it as a competitor to B003. I keep it as an alternative only because Mori and Walter is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, apart from the open question on PERK and ATF6 (Ron, Harding, Kaufman). I also agree with him that a second part would force the GLP-1 credit below three names, with no scientific reason for it. We have a co-authorship history, which I have disclosed, and I note that we have reached the same position by separate reasoning. I do not want that agreement to count for more than it is worth.

responses.point: He argued that a two-person June and Sadelain prize for B018 makes the missing originator, Eshhar, more conspicuous, since it presents the engineering as the discovery. He also noted that the identification of the 7-36 form is a discrete, testable step, and that the dispute should not be treated only as a weakness for Mojsov.
responses.response: His point about B018 changes my view of the cleanest pair. In round 1 I accepted a June and Sadelain pair as cleaner in design terms, but he is right that it makes Eshhar's absence harder to defend, and a trio with Rosenberg at least reflects the clinical proof of gene-engineered T cells. Neither version repairs the missing originator, and that is why B018 stays an alternative. If the committee ever had to give a B018 configuration, I would prefer June, Sadelain and Rosenberg, with a candid statement about Eshhar. I also take his second point. Treating the priority dispute as only a weakness for Mojsov is too simple, since leaving out the identification of the active form would make the physiology story incomplete.

responses.point: He argued that substituting Knudsen would turn the prize into a drug-development award, that the committee should address the Mojsov priority question openly, and that B043 should be the leading alternative only if the committee prefers a basic-science prize, not a second part with B003.
responses.response: I agree on the first two points and I accept that the priority question has to be handled openly. On optogenetics I take his view that it is the leading alternative for a basic-science prize in neuroscience, but I do not see a trio that avoids visible injustice. Channelrhodopsin characterisation and neuronal deployment are separate steps, and any three of the six names omit someone with a credible claim (Bamberg, Boyden or Miesenböck). The clinical use is also still early. I therefore keep B018 and B045 as my alternatives, and I would not support B043 as a second part, which would breach the three-person cap.

uncertainties: Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) form relative to Habener and other early investigators cannot be verified from the supplied files, and every member's view, including mine, rests on recalled knowledge.
Whether the committee frames B003 around physiology and the active peptide or around the therapy, which would reopen the choice between Mojsov and Knudsen.
How the citation and committee statement acknowledge the long-acting analogue programme without crediting it by name.
Whether B018 can be configured fairly without Eshhar, and whether Rosenberg belongs in it.
Long-term safety and the full breadth of benefit of incretin therapy are still being characterised.
statement.conflict_note: I disclose again my roughly twenty co-authored works with fellow member Thomas Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy) and my postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard. None of the credited names on any shortlisted ballot relates to these ties, and I see no need for recusal. As chair I have recorded the chair's questions without a ruling, and my own configuration should not be given extra weight because of that role. My views here do not change the disclosure I gave in round 1.
